reason: I tried to kill this on all four offered grounds and it survives all four, because THIS PANEL ALREADY CONFIRMED IT AND THE STATED REASON FOR NOT SHIPPING IT HAS EXPIRED. Rendered state=print to A4 PDF and to print-media screenshots on paper and ink (byte-identical composition): .b-printLinkLabel 'THE PLAN STAYS ONLINE AT' at y=826 in 11px mono at fore-62, .b-printLinkUrl at y=849, 218px wide, three lines of 13px mono, ending 'yH3cW8pZ5sD0aG7fJ4uE2rN9tM'. The block is the sheet's only route back; nothing else on the paper carries an address. (b) FAILS: the sheet is not a mute keepsake by design - it spends a labelled block on an address, so the artifact itself commits to the reach-back and the only question is whether it can be honoured. (c) FAILS: 'The plan stays online at' is a preposition whose object is a web address; whatever you call it, the sheet hands the reader somewhere to go. (a) FAILS: nothing is protected, the architecture is 'greenfield', the modules are #111111 on #ffffff so no hue, no weight, no family, no radius is added, and the finding already marks itself BUILD, which the round note says goes on the founder's list rather than being made mid-round. (d) FAILS and in fact backfires: the round-5 refuter ruled on the shortening alternative in terms - 'Reject the short code: a case-insensitive id space is a data-model change, out of scope' - so the out-of-scope data model is the reason a scannable route is needed, not a reason to refuse one. PRECEDENT, which is the load-bearing fact. panel/round-5/verdicts/share-url-never-legible.json is real:true and its sharpenedFix is this finding almost verbatim: 'Paper: a QR belongs - modules are #111111 on white, functional signage, not decoration - and needs no external asset: the fixture token is deterministic, so inline it as an SVG rect grid.' Every round-6 seat brief then records why it was not built: 'a QR code on the keepsake was endorsed by a refuter but deliberately NOT shipped, because a QR that does not scan is worse than none and it cannot be verified offline here.' That objection is now false. The repo already depends on qrcode ^1.5.4 (package.json) and already renders QR codes in production at src/components/settings/profile/two-factor-row.tsx:88. I generated the real code offline from the static token: 37x37 modules, ECC M, a 2,378-byte inline SVG, deterministic. NOT A RESTATED GATE and NOT SETTLED: interaction-check.mjs:1854 is named 'the sheet carries a link that can be typed' but asserts only said.link.indexOf('https://') === 0 - the name promises far more than the test proves, which is exactly the gap. SETTLED's printed-url-severs-the-host (round 8) is about where the three lines break, and the-keepsake-has-no-door (round 7) is about in-artifact navigation; neither covers this. Round 11's do-not-file list names only the past-moment edit, not this. THE FIX DOES NOT MAKE IT WORSE - measured, not asserted. I composited the real qrcode SVG into .b-printLink above the URL: at 96px the sheet goes 972px -> 1080px against the gate's 1123px ceiling; at the finding's 28mm/106px it goes to 1090px. Both hold, but 96px is the right number and 28mm is not - it eats 118 of the sheet's 151px of slack for no gain, and 96px is what round 5 specified. Looked at the composite: it reads as ink furniture in the empty foot of the left column, second in mass only to the 79, and it does not fight the hairline language. CORRECTIONS THE SEAT OWES. The URL is 78 characters, not 76 (the 43-character token is right). The distribution story - 'the venue got a printout' while the couple and families hold the chat link - is nowhere in the fixture, the brief or DIRECTIONS.md; the lab calls it only 'the print keepsake', so that paragraph is embroidery and should be struck. The benchmark appeal is wrong on both examples: a Stripe RECEIPT carries no QR (its invoice PDF does), and a ticket's barcode is a gate credential scanned by staff, not a route back to a page. And 'nobody can act on that' is overstated - a determined reader can transcribe 78 case-preserved mono characters, it is just slow and error-prone. Strip all of that and what is left still stands on its own: the sheet makes an offer, the offer costs the reader a minute of error-prone transcription, the panel confirmed the same defect in round 5, and the single reason given for deferring it no longer applies.
sharpenedFix: BUILD, and a small one now that the blocker is gone - roughly an hour, on the founder's list, not made mid-round. In build.mjs, encode F.shareUrlFull with the repo's existing qrcode dependency (QRCode.toString, type 'svg', errorCorrectionLevel 'M', margin 0, dark #111111, light #ffffff) and inline the result - it is 37x37 modules and 2.4KB, deterministic from the static token, so the master stays a single file with no external asset. Emit it inside .b-printLink ABOVE .b-printLinkUrl at 96px square, NOT the finding's 28mm/106px: 96px was round 5's measured number, keeps the sheet at 1080px against the 1123px ceiling, and still gives 0.69mm per module on a home laser. Give the SVG role='img' and aria-label 'Scan to open the plan online' so the screen-shown print state states what it is. Keep the full URL underneath unchanged as the human-readable fallback, and keep the label in the existing micro register - round 5's 'Scan for the live plan' beside 'The plan stays online at', not a second sentence. Then tighten the gate that let this sit: interaction-check.mjs:1854 currently calls indexOf('https://') === 0 'a link that can be typed'; either rename it to what it tests or make it assert the scannable route exists on the sheet.
